blocks.content: A judge of the Supreme Court shall not be removed from his office except by an order of the President passed after an address by each House of Parliament.

rows: President, on address by Parliament with special majority
Same grounds and process as a SC Judge

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Constitutional body heads like CAG, CEC, and UPSC members hold office for 6 years or until 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
Supreme Court judges hold office until 65 years of age, whereas High Court judges hold office until 62 years.
The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President and lacks fixed security of tenure.
Removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament.
UPSC members can be removed by the President only after a Supreme Court inquiry confirms misbehaviour.
Differentiate between offices holding tenure under 'Pleasure of the President' (e.g., Governor, Attorney General) vs 'Security of Tenure' (e.g., CAG, CEC).
Grounds for removal of SC/HC judges and CAG are strictly limited to 'proved misbehaviour' or 'incapacity'.
Note the retirement age difference: Supreme Court Judges (65 years) vs High Court Judges (62 years).
